newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan emperor "grieved at heart" over hostages.
newsitem.headline: Japan emperor "grieved at heart" over hostages.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito, who turned 63 on Monday, voiced deep grief over hundreds of people taken hostage by Marxist rebels in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I would like to tell you that I feel deeply grieved over the fact that those people who attended a party in celebration of my birthday were taken hostage," Akihito told a news conference.
"I ardently hope that everything will be brought under control and that all of the hostages will be released without harm as soon as possible," he added.

About 20 armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas last Tuesday stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima during a party there in honour of Akihito's 63rd birthday, taking hundreds of people hostage.
The hostage crisis forced the Japanese government to cancel all formal events marking Akihito's birthday.
The emperor had planned to hold a party at the Imperial Palace on his birthday, where diplomats, politicians and celebrities were invited.
He was also scheduled to speak from a glassed-in balcony at the palace to well-wishers. The emperor's birthday is a public holiday in Japan.
Akihito ascended the Chrysanthemum Throne in January 1989 after the death of his father, Hirohito.
